prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Meet Your New Desktop Companion", "Verify your pet's appearance and personality before finalizing your adoption."]
1: ["Mastering Desktop Pet Commands", "Learn how to summon, control, and interact with your pet right from your desktop.", "Click pet to open command wheel", "Practice Commands"]
2: ["Save Your Pet Companion", "Sign in now to link your new companion to your account and sync across desktop devices."]
3: ["Tips for Perfect Custom Pet Generation", "Use clear lighting and front-facing photos of your pet for best results.", "Got It, Upload Photo"]
4: ["Log in with your original account to keep existing pets and avoid accidental account resets.", "Sign in to keep your pet data safe and synchronized across desktop devices."]
5: ["Your Pet is Ready! Claim Starter Kit", "Welcome your companion to your desktop and claim 50 free coins for toys and accessories.", "+50 Starter Coins", "Claim & Launch Pet"]
6: ["Choose How to Create Your Pet", "Select a premade companion or upload photos to create a custom pet.", "Premade vs Custom Pet"]
7: ["Configuring Desktop Overlay", "Setting up screen permissions and window boundaries for your pet...", "Verifying Desktop Display Window"]
8: ["Your Desktop Pet is Active!", "Press Alt+P anytime to hide or show your pet. Right-click your pet to open actions and voice chat.", "Tip: You can drag your pet to any position or second monitor."]
9: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets", "Bring your screen to life with an interactive digital pet that keeps you company while you work."]

verdicts.problem: Mentions free extras and virtual currency (free coins).
